title: Privacy-Anchored SSO & HSM Fallback: Scoped Requirements, Scope Change Log, and Sign-off Checklist
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket consolidates product-level requirements, clarifies a requested scope change, records decisions, and collects evidence for sign-off related to SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC enforcement, immutable audit events, and KMS/HSM operator fallback for Private and Dedicated deployments. Goal: produce a clear acceptance bundle that the security/compliance committee and an initial pilot customer can sign off on. The document is intentionally prescriptive about observability and test vectors to minimize ambiguity during engineering implementation and audit evidence collection.
scope_change_log: 2025-11-15: Customer pilot requested support for HSM-backed signing of SAML assertions. Added 'HSM-signing' to scope (impact: cryptographic operator work).
2025-11-20: Reduced initial audit retention requirement from 5 years to 1 year for pilot; final retention decision deferred to compliance gating.
2025-11-28: Scope clarified to require per-tenant KMS CMK (customer-managed key) wrapping for stored KV caches in Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: SAML metadata ingestion and verification must support signed metadata and validate certificate chains; automated metadata refresh can be scheduled and must detect signature expiry within 24 hours and create an alert.
OIDC: Issuer discovery and JWKS rotation handling must tolerate up to 10s JWKS propagation delay and fallback to cached JWKS for up to 6 hours with audit annotation.
RBAC: Platform API enforces role-to-action mapping at the gateway layer; negative test cases must prove privilege escalation is blocked (test vectors included in test_plan).

Audit logs: Immutable append-only audit stream exported to customer-owned S3 (or equivalent) with cryptographic signing of blocks; retention and export proof for 365 days must be demonstrable in the pilot.
KMS/HSM: Support CMK import policy flags that prevent key material export; HSM-backed signing for assertion-level signatures must operate with <50ms additional signing latency under test load.

HSM fallback: If HSM cluster becomes unreachable, the operator must be able to promote a pre-authorized software-backed signing key for emergency signing with full audit annotation and must support automatic rollback when HSM recovers.
Operational: Playbook for key rotation (CMK) must include steps for pre-rotation snapshot, controlled roll-forward, and post-rotation integrity checks with observable metrics recorded in Console.
Evidence: Each acceptance item must include a linked artifact (PR, Confluence runbook, test run, dashboard) and a named reviewer who signed off in comments.
test_plan: Functional test: End-to-end SAML login through customer's IdP with signed assertion verification and assertion timestamp drift tests (+/- 2 minutes).
Load test: Measure HSM signing p95 latency under 200 concurrent signing requests; document fallback latency when HSM is unreachable.
Security test: RBAC fuzzing suite against route table and token exchange endpoints; produce exploit attempt log and mitigation evidence.
Audit test: Simulate bulk audit export and verify cryptographic block chain and S3 object immutability via hash verification script (artifact attached).
decisions: Adopt per-tenant CMK model for Private deployments; platform-managed key option remains for hosted service only.
HSM signing will be implemented as an optional operator-configured module; software fallback requires explicit customer opt-in and an operator-run emergency checklist.
Audit stream will be based on append-only blocks signed by a rotating platform key; customer export will include signed manifests for integrity verification.
implementation_notes: ENG: Prioritize SAML metadata validation library upgrade to support RFC-compliant signature algorithms and certificate revocation checks.
ENG: KV cache encryption must accept externally-wrapped keys from customer CMK; update key-wrapping API and key-usage metadata tags.
ENG: Add Console visibility for 'key-state' and 'hsm-availability' with alerting thresholds and recorded incident metrics.

Follow-up: After pilot sign-off, schedule a post-mortem / evidence review within 30 days to capture drift and any configuration edge cases encountered.
